question.problem: If $[a]_{n}$ denotes the residue class containing all integers congruent to $a$ modulo $n,$ then $[-29]_{9}=$
question.worked_solution:
We have $[a]_{9}=[b]_{9}$ if 

$$
a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,9).
$$

The residue class $[-29]_{9}$ consists of the elements that are congruent to $-29$ modulo $9.$ 

We can find an alternative representation for this residue class as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[-29]_{9} & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡-29\,(\text{mod}\,9)\} \\  & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡(-4)\cdot 9+7\,(\text{mod}\,9)\} \\  & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡(-4)\cdot 0+7\,(\text{mod}\,9)\} \\  & =\{x\in Z\,|\,x≡7\,(\text{mod}\,9)\} \\  & =[7]_{9}\end{aligned}
$$
